Sweep density thresholds for robustness assessment

Source: R/comparison.R
density_sweep.Rd

Reruns the pairwise comparison at several threshold multipliers. Shows how sensitive the conservation results are to the density cutoff.

Usage

density_sweep(networks, ...)

# Default S3 method
density_sweep(
  networks,
  orthologs,
  multipliers = seq(0.95, 1.05, by = 0.01),
  method = c("permutation", "hypergeometric", "rank"),
  n_cores = 1L,
  use_torch = FALSE,
  pval_combine = c("max", "min"),
  seed = NULL,
  rho0 = NULL,
  null_networks = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

networks

Named list of compute_network() outputs.

...

Additional arguments passed to the default method.

orthologs

Data frame with columns gene1, gene2, hog.

multipliers

Numeric vector of threshold multipliers (default seq(0.95, 1.05, by = 0.01)).

method

Comparison method passed to find_coexpressologs(): "permutation" (default), "hypergeometric" or "rank".

n_cores

Number of threads (default 1).

use_torch

Logical; GPU acceleration for permutation method (default FALSE).

pval_combine

Passed to find_coexpressologs(): "max" (default) requires both directions to be significant (the reciprocal criterion of Netotea et al. (2014)); "min" calls a pair when either direction is significant.

seed

Integer seed for the sweep's random draws, or NULL (default) to draw from the global RNG. Applied once here, so the whole sweep is one reproducible unit: the multipliers are visited in order and each find_coexpressologs() call continues the same stream, which keeps a level's draws independent of its neighbours' while making the sweep as a whole repeatable. Because nothing is drawn before the first multiplier, a sweep seeded with s reproduces find_coexpressologs(seed = s) exactly at its first level. See find_coexpressologs() for what a seed does and does not pin under each method.

rho0

Passed to find_coexpressologs(): reference fold enrichment for the analytical power column.

null_networks

Passed to find_coexpressologs() (rank method only); every null's threshold is scaled by the same multiplier as its species' network.

Value

A data frame with columns multiplier, eff_density, n_significant, edges (list-column of edge data frames), and species_densities (list-column of named numeric vectors giving the effective density per species at each threshold level).

Details

For each multiplier, every network's threshold is scaled by threshold * multiplier, the effective density is recorded, and find_coexpressologs() is called on the modified networks.

See also

find_coexpressologs(), classify_cliques

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sweep <- density_sweep(networks, orthologs,
  method = "permutation", use_torch = TRUE
)
} # }
